summary: Read-only `git branch -a` is blocked as a mutation in a no-modification task
explanation: When the user says not to modify files, Reasonix 1.24.1 enforces a no-mutation task policy (agent/taskpolicy_gate.go). Its command classifier (evidence/evidence.go) does not recognise `git branch -a` as a read-only listing, so the bash call is refused with `blocked: task policy forbids mutation`, after the permission prompt was already approved. Evidence requirement: a bash tool call whose command is `git branch -a` (or equivalent pure listing) in a turn under the no-modification constraint, and its tool result `blocked: task policy forbids mutation`. A refusal of a command that does mutate, or a permission denial, does not establish this defect.
expected_behavior: Pure listing commands such as `git branch -a` run under a no-modification constraint; only mutating commands are refused.
observed_behavior: In 10 of 10 independent runs on 1.24.1, `git branch -a` was approved at the permission prompt and then returned `blocked: task policy forbids mutation`.
